attributes.readMe:
# Contractor

## Summary
A contractor resource linked from Offers and Projects. Extends PersonBase with `status` (active | inactive | terminated), `billableRate` (hourly/daily rate in dollars), `vatId` (for invoicing), `invoiceFrequency` (monthly | quarterly | annually), a contract window (`contractStartDate` / `contractEndDate`), and `vendor` / `project` links (the agency they come through, the project they are staffed on). Two derived fields hang off the window: `daysRemaining` (a SIGNED computed NumberField — negative once expired, undefined when open-ended) and `expiryLabel` (a denormalized computed StringField: "23d left" / "ends today" / "expired" / '' when open-ended). `title` is computed from `name`.

## Import
```ts
import { Contractor, expiryTone, EXPIRY_TONE_COLORS } from './contractor';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As the external resource pool.** Contractors are linked from Offers as alternative hiring paths — when a requisition is filled via contract labor instead of permanent hire, the offer points at a Contractor instance instead of creating an Employee record.

**2. As the invoicing source.** The `billableRate`, `invoiceFrequency`, and `vatId` drive invoice generation; the billing system queries contractors by `invoiceFrequency` to batch-generate monthly/quarterly/annual invoices.

**3. As the project staffing model.** `project` links the contractor to the Project they are staffed on and `vendor` to the agency supplying them; the project dashboard shows billable cost alongside headcount, and the vendor's rate card can be sanity-checked against `billableRate`.

**4. As a contract-renewal alarm.** `daysRemaining`/`expiryLabel` drive an amber treatment inside 30 days and red once expired (`expiryTone` + `EXPIRY_TONE_COLORS`, the same `stateColor` dilution every other status pill uses). The alert shows in every format: isolated Contract panel, embedded/atom expiry chip, and the fitted tile.

**5. As the Talent & Resource Tracker's Contractors tab.** The tracker (talent-resource-tracker.gts) does NOT hold contractors in a linksToMany — it runs a live `getCards` query for every Contractor in the realm and renders them through `@context.searchResultsComponent` as a prerendered fitted grid, so new contractors appear the moment they are created.

## Template Usage
Isolated displays contact info, rate & terms, and a Contract panel (status, start/end dates, days remaining with the amber/red urgency treatment, vendor and project atoms, VAT ID) in a 2-column layout. Embedded is a one-liner with avatar, name, status pill, and an expiry chip that only appears inside the 30-day window. Fitted degrades through tiers: name → rate + expiry label → end-date/invoice/VAT facts. Atom is the name plus the urgent-only expiry chip.

**Why `expiryLabel` exists (fitted-safe denormalization):** prerendered fitted must not read links, and re-deriving urgency from `contractEndDate` in every consumer invites drift. `expiryLabel` and `daysRemaining` are the contractor's OWN attributes, computed once next to the data — the fitted tile, embedded chip, and atom chip all read the same two scalars, so a tile and the isolated view can never disagree about how urgent the same end date is. `daysRemaining` is deliberately signed (utils' `daysBetween` clamps at 0, which would erase "ended three weeks ago" into "ends today"). The same rationale added `vendorName` and `projectName` — denormalized computed copies of the linked vendor's and project's names — so the tall fitted tiers can name the agency and engagement without a link read.

## Examples
- `Contractor/sarah-chen` — active, $95/hr monthly, contract window 2026-02-01 → 2026-09-01 via TalentBridge Agency on Platform Rebuild; inside the 30-day window, so she demonstrates the amber expiry treatment everywhere.
- `Contractor/marcus-rodriguez` — active, $120/hr quarterly, window 2026-05-15 → 2027-02-15 via TalentBridge Agency on Benefits Migration; months out, so no alert renders — the quiet baseline case.

## Reuse notes
Contractors reuse the PersonBase avatar/initials/name infrastructure so they render consistently across the app. Contract status colors (active=green, inactive=amber, terminated=red) follow the same v1 pattern as Employee and Candidate statuses.

**Non-goals:** Contract documents/file storage (separate document management); billable hours tracking (belongs in time-tracking integration); benefit eligibility (Contractors are out-of-scope for benefits); auto-renewal workflow (the alert surfaces the decision, a human makes it).
